subject: CPathFind AI navigation — node grid, link table, and ped/vehicle path queries
overview: GTA:SA's AI pathfinding uses a pre-baked node graph stored in data/paths/NODES.DAT (and separate PEDNODES.DAT). Nodes are 3D waypoints; links between nodes encode speed limits, road type, and lane flags. Vehicles follow node paths to navigate traffic; peds follow ped-specific node paths. The CPathFind singleton owns the node and link arrays and exposes query functions.

CPathFind_singleton.description: Singleton pointer. Accessing [CPathFind+offset] gives fields on the singleton.

CPathNode_layout.description: Each traffic node in NODES.DAT. Nodes are 28 bytes.

fields.name: m_nAreaID
fields.description: Which streaming area (IPL tile) this node belongs to

fields.name: m_nNodeID
fields.description: Index of this node within its area

fields.name: m_wLinkID
fields.description: Index into the link table for this node's first link

fields.name: m_nNumLinks
fields.description: Number of outgoing links from this node

fields.name: m_nPathWidth
fields.description: Road width at this node (in 0.5m increments)

fields.name: m_nFlags0
fields.description: Packed flags: speed limit, road type, junction flag, don't wander flag

fields.name: m_nFlags1
fields.description: Additional flags: flood prevention, road blocked, water crossing

CPathLink_layout.description: Each directed link between two path nodes.

fields.name: m_wNodeID
fields.description: Target node index within that area

fields.name: m_nFlags
fields.description: Link flags: direction, bridge, traffic light approach

m_nFlags0_bits.bit_4: Is junction (intersection node — traffic light and give-way checks)
m_nFlags0_bits.bit_5: Is disabled (no vehicle will use this node)

NODES_DAT.description: Binary file containing all vehicle path nodes. Split into 64×64 areas; each area is 400×400 game units.

PEDNODES_DAT.description: Binary file for ped-only navigation. Same format but with tighter node spacing and footpath/staircase special flags.

CPathFind_FindNodeClosestToCoors.description: Find the nearest path node to a world position; used by vehicle AI to get on-road

CPathFind_DoPathSearch.description: A* pathfinding: returns a chain of nodes from start to goal

CPathFind_GetRandomNodeNearPosition.description: Get a random nearby node; used for ambient traffic destination selection

CPathFind_FindNthNodeClosestToCoors.description: Get the Nth nearest node; used when the first is blocked or occupied
